title: Count the Real Mailboxes

concept.title: Normalise first, then put into a set
body: Several different-looking texts can mean the same thing. The trick for counting the **really different** ones is to convert each text to a **normal form** (a fixed way of writing it) and put the normal forms in a set. The size of the set is the answer.

body.code:
local, domain = email.split("@")
local = local.split("+")[0].replace(".", "")
normal = local + "@" + domain

body: The rules here: in the part before the `@`, dots do not matter, and everything from the first `+` on is ignored. The part after the `@` (the domain) is used exactly as written.

statement: An email address is a local part, an `@` and a domain. In the local part, all dots are ignored, and the first `+` and everything after it (up to the `@`) is ignored. The domain is not changed. Two addresses reach the same mailbox if they are equal after these rules. Given `n` addresses, count how many different mailboxes they reach.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` addresses (each without spaces).
outputFormat: Print the number of different mailboxes.
constraints: Each address has one `@`, a local part of letters, dots and `+` that starts with a letter, and a domain of lowercase letters and dots.
Each address has at most 40 characters.

examples.note: The first two are the mailbox testemail@mail.com; the third has another domain: 2 mailboxes.

hints: Cut the local part at the first `+` and remove all dots.
Put the normal form into a set; the answer is the size of the set.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
e = input().split()

# Your code here

explanation: Each address is converted to its normal form (no dots, cut at `+`, same domain); the set of normal forms counts the mailboxes.
solution.complexity: Time O(total length), space O(total length).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
e = input().split()

unique = set()
for email in e:
    local, domain = email.split("@")
    local = local.split("+")[0].replace(".", "")
    unique.add(local + "@" + domain)
print(len(unique))
